sections.title: Construction Inspection
sections.summary: Inspector verifies construction conforms to plans and specifications. Key activities: verify material certifications and corrosion protection integrity; monitor driven soldier beam plumb; verify drilled-in beam hole dimensions and backfill; confirm drill hole dimensions, cleanliness, and orientation; verify tendon unbonded and bond lengths and centralizer spacing; witness grouting (continuous flow, pressure monitored); witness anchor tests per Chapter 7; verify lagging dimensions and backpacking. Performance monitoring includes anchor load cells and wall movement surveys.
sections.body:
Inspector role: The inspector is the primary mechanism to assure construction conforms to project plans and specifications. For the performance approach, the contractor is responsible for system performance, but the owner's inspector provides independent oversight. For design-build, the contractor conducts or is responsible for all required inspection activities; the owner provides independent quality assurance.

Material inspection: Steel elements (sheet piles, soldier beams) accepted based on mill certificates. Timber lagging: verify dimensions and species/grade. Ground anchor tendons: verify corrosion protection continuity (encapsulation undamaged; grout completely filling sheaths; epoxy coating unbroken; trumpet and cover properly fitted). Non-conforming materials must be rejected or replaced unless approved in writing by the project engineer.

Vertical wall element installation: Drilled-in soldier beams — verify hole dimensions, structural/lean-mix concrete backfill; inclinometer casing installation if specified. Driven soldier beams — monitor alignment and plumbness; if excessively damaged, may require replacement with drilled-in beam.

Anchor hole drilling: Verify hole diameter, depth, inclination, and alignment. Drill hole is considered clean if the full length of the tendon can be easily inserted to the desired depth. Verify hole is drilled to full design depth and grouted promptly after drilling.

Tendon installation: Verify that minimum bond and unbonded lengths are equal to or exceed specified values. Verify centralizer/spacer installation. For bar tendons, verify coupler installation where applicable.

Grouting: Grout injected at the lowest point in the drill hole to fill without air voids. Grout must flow continuously as the grout tube, auger, or casing is withdrawn — withdrawal rate must be less than grout placement rate. Grouting equipment must include a pressure gauge; verify grout pressure and volume. After testing and lock-off, fill trumpet with grout and place cover; verify complete filling after grout sets.

Lagging installation: Timber lagging must be the proper thickness (per Table 12) and placed with proper louver gaps. Voids behind lagging must be backpacked promptly to prevent soil raveling.

Anchor testing: Inspector witnesses all performance, proof, and extended creep tests. Test measurements should be plotted as the test proceeds to identify unusual behavior. Applied load must not be reduced below the alignment load during a test.

Performance monitoring: Wall movements monitored by survey or inclinometer during construction. Anchor loads monitored by load cells. Outward wall movement and significant load increase in anchor may indicate ground is weaker than anticipated; if anchor load approaches maximum test load, detension to design load and investigate.
key_points: Verify tendon corrosion protection integrity: no damage to encapsulation, grout fills sheaths, epoxy coatings unbroken
Grout must flow continuously during withdrawal; withdrawal rate < grout placement rate; air voids not acceptable
Anchor test measurements plotted in real time to identify unusual behavior; load must never drop below alignment load
Timber lagging: proper thickness per Table 12; backpack voids behind lagging immediately
Monitor anchor loads during construction; outward movement + load increase → investigate possible weak ground condition
sections.applicability: Construction inspection checklist and performance monitoring for anchored wall projects
